correctness.rationale: For C⁴ once-traversed planar simple γ of length L with 0<r<reach(γ), tube geometry gives S=2πrL, V=πr²L, rho=L/(2πr)>1. Principal curvatures and angular integral establish W=π/(2r)∫[1−r²κ(s)²]^−1/2 ds; with ∫κ ds=2π and q=2πr/L, supporting-line convexity of g(z)=(1−z)^−1/2 proves the claimed exact envelope π²rho²/sqrt(rho²−1) and global curvature deficit πr/[4(1−q²)^(3/2)]∫(κ−2π/L)². Equality forces constant signed curvature, hence circle. For strictly convex support perturbations h=R+εf with zero mean/first modes, ds=(h+h″)dφ, F(p)=p²/sqrt(p²−r²), F″(R)=r²(R²+2r²)/(R²−r²)^(5/2), giving specified quadratic coefficient; Fourier (k²−1)²≥9, attained only k=2. Independent symbolic derivative and numerical R=2,r=.8 noncircular perturbation give W≈26.923369, circular ≈26.921553, gap ≈.001816 above variance lower ≈.001155. Numeric examples do not prove global validity.

value.rationale: Constant-radius planar tubes are a natural geometrically constrained torus family. The proof identifies the unique optimizing circle under physical S,V constraints, a quantitative excess-energy control for all embedded planar cores, and an exact spectral least-penalized mode for near-circle perturbations; it answers a motivated classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The simple forward integral alone would not satisfy value, but simultaneous sharp constrained classification and stability do.
